newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Asbrink wants to review rules on pensions.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Asbrink wants to review rules on pensions.

text.p: The Swedish government wants to conduct a broad review of the rules governing investments by state pension funds and insurance companies, Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said.
"The objective of the review is to achieve a better functioning capital market," Asbrink told journalists after a budget debate in parliament.
During the debate Asbrink said he thought it was extraordinary for American pension funds to be allowed to buy Swedish company shares when Swedish pension funds were prevented from doing so.

The three largest Swedish pension funds, whose assets total more than 550 billion Swedish crowns, are at present obliged by law to invest 97 percent in interest-bearing government securities, and the remaining three percent in property.

Asbrink suggested last week that those funds should in future be allowed to invest also in Swedish shares, adding that this would not only diversify the portofolio but guard against excessive foreign ownership of Swedish listed companies.
